problem: Two documentation lists restated what the code already knew, and one was already wrong: docs/CAPABILITIES.md described about twenty capabilities while the registry held 58, missing every screen.*, network.*, display.*, input.* and system.service* entry added that day. A reader trusts a documentation file, so a wrong one costs more than an absent one. Separately, the day produced one bug shape five times in five subsystems and it was at risk of being recorded as five unrelated bugs.
change: Made the capability table generated by ./scripts/aries-capability-docs, which rewrites only what sits between two markers and leaves the hand-written prose alone, with a --check mode that exits 1 when stale. Added tests/test_docs.py to gate it in the suite. Wrote docs/SPEECH.md to the project's per-subsystem convention. Recorded entries 018 to 027 in docs/ERROR_LOG.md, including a new recurring section 'Exit zero is not evidence' and a second on hand-maintained lists drifting.
validation: The gate was proven to bite rather than merely to pass: removing one generated row from docs/CAPABILITIES.md made --check exit 1 and made tests/test_docs.py fail naming screen.read; restoring the file returned ALL PASSED. One of the six checks deliberately distrusts the generator, reading the registry and the file independently, because --check compares the file to the generator's own output and a generator that silently dropped a row would agree with itself forever. Every factual claim in docs/SPEECH.md was checked against the running code rather than memory: default engines per language, the speak() signature, that ARIES_SPEECH_MK_FALLBACK is honoured, that engines.engine('mk','piper') raises by name, that both fetch scripts are executable, and that bench.py accepts the flags the document cites. tests/test_docs.py 6 checks ALL PASSED.
limitations: The generated description column is each Capability's own description, which says less about independent observation than the hand-written column did for the entries it covered; a complete table that cannot drift was judged better than a richer one that was two-thirds absent, and that is a trade rather than a win. --check is not yet wired into any CI outside the test suite. The ERROR_LOG conventions are written but nothing enforces them; only the exit-zero one has a mechanical counterpart, in the per-capability verifiers that already existed. docs/CAPABILITIES.md still ends with a hand-written paragraph stating there is deliberately no shell capability in the registry, which will contradict the code if the shell capability written this session is ever registered.
